newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end higher, earnings provide boost.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end higher, earnings provide boost.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished broadly higher on Thursday, with the Dow industrials rebounding from sharp losses on Wednesday and Nasdaq rolling to its sixth consecutive record.
The Dow gained 44 points to close unofficially at 7887. Advancing issues beat decliners by a seven-to-four margin on the NYSE, where volume topped 500 million shares.
Blue chips were again buoyed by solid earnings news, this time from General Electric Co, which reported a record profit of $2.16 billion in the second quarter.
GE's earnings of $0.66 per share also beat consensus estimates by a penny, making the Dow component the third this week to beat Wall Street expectations. Shares in GE climbed 1-1/16 to 69-1/2.
The early returns, particularly from blue chip companies, had some analysts voicing optimism about the quarter.

"Most of the negative feelings that existed coming into this quarter seemed to center on fears of higher interest rates and the impact of a too-strong dollar," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "Neither of those really developed."

Tech stocks continued their torrid gains, overcoming a weak showing by chip bellwether Intel Corp, which fell 2-1/2 to 150-1/8 after Salomon Brothers analyst Erika Klauer voiced caution about the company's upcoming results.
Investors opted to focus on the bigger picture, however, looking past Intel's problems, which largely involve issues related to its transition to a new generation of chips.

For now, the broader view is a fairly rosy one. Of the 96 companies reporting earnings through July 10, 54.2 percent have beaten expectations while only 29.2 have fallen short of estimates, according to Zacks Investment Research.
The pace of pleasant surprises is off slightly from a year ago, which several analysts noted reflected high expectations in the market.

"It doesn't appear we're going to have quite as big a surprise factor," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker. "That could take away some of the momentum that had been created in the market."
The result could be more of the choppy, sideways activity that has gripped the Dow since its sizzling 223-point run heading into the Independence Day holiday.
Since that time, the blue chip average has swung wildly, gyrating in 100-point or larger bands in each session. Yet it has only given up a total of nine points during that period.
While the volatility had made for some unsettling moments, analysts said it has served a purpose.
"I think if we head into a period of back-and-forth consolidation it would be a positive for this market," Cripps said. "We had such a huge move, it's reasonable to see the market take a rest."
Within the sideways market, pockets of furious activity continue to surface.
International Paper Co surged 3-1/16 to 58 to lead Dow advancers, extending a rally since the company reported stronger than expected earnings and announced a restructuring on Tuesday.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc rose 1-7/16 to 35-1/16. The retailer was one of several to report strong June sales, with comparable-store sales up 6.4 percent in the month.
Marvel Entertainment Group Inc rose 1/8 to 2-3/8 after the company reached agreement on a meger with Toy Biz Inc.
The deal, which was approved by Marvel's banks and bondholders, may spell an end to months of bitter litigation and enable Marvel to emerge from bankruptcy by fall.
Toy Biz shares jumped 1-5/16 to 9-5/16.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 4.30 points to 1490.93.
The S&P 500 index rose 6.24 points to 913.78.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
